text:
Samir: quick summary from the horizon13b int6 pilot (TL;DR at top)

Samir: ran a focused 2.5k-sample pilot on our longform/multi-turn (>1000 tokens) slice. Major takeaways: ~48% token cost reduction, p95 latency down ~22%, but recall@5 on long-context factuals fell by ~3.6pp.

Nina: drop the slice table + raw numbers please, and which prompts regressed?

Samir: paste of the slice metrics (baseline f16 vs int6):
```
slice: longform-multiturn-1000+
samples: 2500
baseline (f16): cost_per_1k_tokens = $0.14 | p95_latency = 980ms | recall@5 = 80.2%
int6:                 cost_per_1k_tokens = $0.073 | p95_latency = 765ms | recall@5 = 76.6%
delta:                                             -47.9% cost | -21.9% p95 | -3.6pp recall
```

Ryan: is the degradation uniform or focused? any obvious failure modes?

Samir: focused. failure clusters: 1) numeric/date extraction in regulatory/legal scenarios, 2) multi-paragraph cross-references ("see paragraph 4 above"), 3) complex inline code blocks with mixed punctuation. single-turn short QA and summarization lt;200 tokens looked fine.

Alice: product ask — what routing do we recommend for GTM? default int6 or more conservative?

Samir: propose hybrid routing with simple rules:
- short (<=150 tokens): int6
- medium (151-500): int6 canary 30%
- long (>500) OR flagged_sensitive (legal/finance/rerank): float16/int8
- automatic fallback: if recall@5 drops >2.0pp OR hallucination_rate >1.3x baseline -> route to int8
- rollout cadence: 3% non-critical traffic for 48h, then 15% for 7 days with daily checks, then 30% with extended monitoring

Carol: GTM needs a crisp per-request savings number and risk bullets. can you give unit-econ quick math?

Samir: unit-econ (rounded):
- avg tokens per request on this slice = 610
- baseline cost per 1k tokens = $0.14 -> baseline cost per req ≈ $0.0854
- int6 cost per 1k tokens = $0.073 -> int6 cost per req ≈ $0.0445
- saving per req ≈ $0.041 (~48% reduction)
- at 2M requests/month -> ≈ $82k saved on this slice (ballpark, recompute per-product mix before publishing)

Nina: canary metrics to wire (my suggested): recall@5 (slice), p95_latency, tokens_per_call, error/timeout rate, hallucination_rate, user_flag_rate. add a product proxy: engagement on suggestions for a week. also add automated alerts if recall delta >1.5pp for any critical slice.

Ryan: saw quant artifacts around punctuation and numeric formatting. mitigation ideas: pre/post normalizers for dates/numbers and target small model tweak (tokenizer priming) for templated code blocks. cheap stopgap: structured post-process for finance/legal extractions.

Lee: i'll add a small synthetic suite for those legal/regression cases to the daily job. alarm if failures exceed 2% absolute.

deploy-bot: scheduled-deploy: canary-int6/horizon13b -> 2024-07-22 03:00 UTC (3% traffic) — monitors: recall_delta_longform, p95_latency, hallucination_rate, tokens_per_call

Alice: who owns rollout doc + GTM one-pager?

Samir: i'll author the rollout doc + canary dashboards (Samir). Carol will draft the GTM one-pager with unit-econ tables (Carol). Nina + Lee will own the slice tests and post-process hooks. target: canary live Mon, initial readout after 1 week ramp.

Carol: i'll include sensitivity rows for token count, traffic mix, and an alert section describing worst-case costs and rollback triggers.

Nina: wiring alarms now. threshold proposal: pause canary if recall drop >2.5pp on the long slice OR hallucination_rate >1.4x baseline. I'll also add a daily diff report for top failing prompts.

Samir: downstream note — if product needs stricter SLAs for legal/finance, we should gate those flows to float16 by default and only allow int6 under explicit opt-in. otherwise we expose too much risk.

Carol: good call. i'll flag that in GTM messaging and the support playbook.

Lee: small ops note — patch the numeric normalizer early in the canary to reduce false positives on our alarms; it's low risk and can be toggled.

Samir: thanks everyone. ping me directly if you see >3pp regression on any other slice and we'll hit the global pause. :eyes: :thumbsup:
